text:
alex: heads up — started seeing a bunch of small gpu pods Pending after last night's scale-up, even though new nodes show available GPUs. :eyes:
maria: same, noticed 30 pods stuck in Pending in eu-west2, mostly 1-GPU jobs. kube-scheduler says fit failed, but nodes have free GPU capacity.
rui: can you paste the scheduler error? sometimes it's a device-plugin registration race after node join.
alex: pasted snippets —
```
scheduler: failed to fit pod: 0/24 nodes are available: 12 Insufficient gpu, 8 node(s) didn't match Pod's nodeSelector, 4 kubelet not ready.
```
maria: interesting — 12 Insufficient gpu but k8s `nvidia.com/gpu` shows free on some nodes. I suspect fragmentation: some nodes only have fractional MIG profiles reserved by other tenants.
sanjay: also saw `NodeAllocatableOverrides` kicked in for the new nodes during warmup. GPUs appear but driver init delays until kubelet config done -> pods see Insufficient at schedule time.
devops-bot: cluster-autoscaler: ScaleUp triggered for nodepool-eu-gpu-spot (2 -> 6). Nodes registering, waiting for kubelet readiness.
alex: that matches. CA spun up a mix of spot and on-demand nodes with different MIG sizes; scheduler can't pack because pods request 1 full GPU and some nodes are fragmented into 7g/5g MIG slices.
rui: quick check: `kubectl get nodes -l cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool=nodepool-eu-gpu-spot -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}:{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Ready")].status}:{.capacity.nvidia.com/gpu}\n'` showed a few nodes Ready but capacity `0` until driver init completes.
maria: for immediate relief, can we 1) temporarily cordon the newly added fragmented nodes, 2) drain small pending jobs onto on-demand full-gpu nodes, or 3) let CA add a small pre-warmed pool with uniform MIG config?
sanjay: option 3 is longer term but better. For now I'd do cordon+drain for nodes that aren't fully registered. Also increase `--scale-down-utilization-threshold` so CA doesn't rip out the on-demand pool too quickly.
alex: doing cordon now on nodepool-eu-gpu-spot-abc123. will `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`.
maria: heads-up: draining will evict some large training jobs. prefer to `kubectl cordon` first and only drain small ones.
alex: agreed. cordoned. re-scheduling started, some pods moved to on-demand pool. Pending count down from 30 -> 6.
rui: logging note: scheduler logs show `PredicateFailed: NodeGpuFragmented` — that's our custom check in the admission plugin to avoid mixing MIG profiles. maybe too strict now.
sanjay: we added that plugin to prevent noisy-neighbor MIG mixes, but it's blocking packing efficiency for 1-GPU jobs. Could relax the plugin to allow best-effort packing for <=1 GPU requests with `allowMixedMig=true` flag.
maria: cost trade-off: relaxing increases chance of interference vs lowering latency/cost by better binpacking. ops asked to keep tail latency guarantees for enterprise customers.
alex: proposal: change scheduler policy for small batch queue (namespace `batch-small`) to prefer binpack across nodes that have homogeneous free full-gpu resources. Keep strict anti-mix for `enterprise/` namespaces.
sanjay: we should also add a tiny pre-warm on-demand nodepool with pinned MIG profile (1g) for short jobs. reserve 4 nodes in eu-west2 as burst capacity. That avoids CA races and driver warmup.
rui: one-off fix: patch cluster-autoscaler config to prefer on-demand for scale-up when there are >10 pending small-gpu pods. `--expander=priority` + priorities map can help.
maria: recorded a quick runbook in #incidents: steps to cordon/drain, check device plugin logs (`kubectl -n kube-system logs -l app=nvidia-device-plugin`), and CA commands to pin scale-up preference.
alex: FYI paste of device-plugin log showing delayed registration:
```
I0308 03:12:15.123456 1 device_plugin.go:200] Registered device plugin: nvidia-device-plugin v0.11
E0308 03:12:20.654321 1 plugin.go:98] failed to setup MIG topology: some GPUs not ready
I0308 03:12:24.000000 1 device_plugin.go:345] All devices reported, capacity updated
```
maria: timeline estimate: ~10-30s between node Ready and GPU capacity visible historically, but this run showed 2-3 minutes due to driver retries.
sanjay: long-term items: (a) pre-warmed homogeneous nodepool for small jobs (b) relax migration predicate for <=1 GPU or add scheduling broker that can pack fractional MIG slots (c) improve CA expander policy to avoid mixing spot/on-demand for same workload.
rui: +1. Also add a check in rollout that new node images have device-plugin pre-installed to speed registration.
alex: opened infra ticket INFRA-7421 to track pre-warm pool + scheduler policy changes. assigning to @sanjay and @rui.
maria: thanks — I'll follow up with cost numbers for reserved pre-warm vs current spot mix. initial calc: 4 pre-warm on-demand nodes adds ~8% monthly infra cost but reduces ~40% scheduling failures for small batches.
devops-bot: created ticket INFRA-7421, linked CA logs. :white_check_mark:
alex: ok closing this thread for now — pods mostly moved. keep monitoring and we'll implement long-term changes. :wave:
maria: leaving notes in eng-infra runbook. ping me if pending > 5 again. :thumbsup:
